caption:
A smaller armhole gives the arm more freedom than a bigger one, according to three tailoring writers.

With a high, narrow armhole the arm moves while the chest and shoulders of the jacket stay put. A low one leaves spare cloth under the arm, and the whole coat rides up when the arms are lifted. The craft is in easing a larger sleeve into the small opening, which takes handwork. Jacomet of Parisian Gentleman suggests a test: raise your arms as if hanging a picture, and a good jacket does not move.

Connected to the drape cut, Anderson & Sheppard, Neapolitan tailoring and Frederick Scholte.
